extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: A dataset of 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both retrieval-based and word co-occurrence algorithms) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The dataset is designed to encourage AI research in advanced question answering requiring knowledge and reasoning beyond surface-level cues.
extraction.creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence
extraction.citeAs: Peter Clark, Isaac Cowhey, Oren Etzioni, Tushar Khot, Ashish Sabharwal, Carissa Schoenick, Oyvind Tafjord. Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457v1 [cs.AI] 14 Mar 2018
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset consists of 7,787 natural science questions drawn from a variety of sources including standardized tests. Questions were collected through several months of extensive search and investigation of public examination materials. The dataset includes questions authored for human standardized tests targeting grade levels 3-9 (students typically age 8-13 years).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were drawn from various standardized test sources including: ACTAAP (Arkansas Comprehensive Testing, Assessment, and Accountability Program), AIMS (Arizona's Instrument to Measure Standards), Alaska Department of Education & Early Development, California Standards Test, FCAT (Florida Comprehensive Assessment Test), Louisiana Department of Education, Maryland School Assessment, MCAS (Massachusetts Comprehensive Assessment System), MEA (Maine Educational Assessment), MEAP (Michigan Educational Assessment Program), Mercury (anonymous content partner), MSA (Maryland School Assessment), NAEP (National Assessment of Educational Progress), NC READY (Ready North Carolina), NY Regents (New York State Educational Department Regents exams), Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS (Texas Assessment of Knowledge and Skills), TIMSS (1995, 2003, 2007, & 2011 Assessments), Virginia Standards of Learning, and WASL (Washington Assessment of Student Learning).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set. Challenge questions were operationally defined as those answered incorrectly by both an Information Retrieval (IR) solver and a Pointwise Mutual Information (PMI) solver. The IR solver searches for explicit statements of question+answer in a corpus, while the PMI solver measures statistical associations between question and answer n-grams.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Questions were filtered to include only non-diagram, multiple-choice questions (typically 4-way multiple choice). The dataset was partitioned into train/dev/test splits with Challenge Set containing 1119/299/1172 questions and Easy Set containing 2251/570/2376 questions respectively.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Questions were originally authored by human test creators for standardized examinations. The correct answers were provided as part of the original test materials.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset contains only non-diagram questions, excluding visual reasoning tasks. Questions vary in difficulty within grade levels, with substantial overlap in difficulty among different grade levels. Simple retrieval and co-occurrence methods perform poorly on the Challenge Set (near random baseline), indicating these questions require more advanced reasoning methods. The dataset is limited to science domain questions from US elementary and middle school curricula.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for training, testing, and validation of question answering systems that require advanced reasoning capabilities beyond simple retrieval or word correlation. The Challenge Set specifically targets development of methods for questions requiring knowledge integration, multi-hop reasoning, and deeper text comprehension. The dataset can be used with the optional ARC Corpus (14M science sentences) or other knowledge sources.
